summary: John B. Cobb Jr. is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago. He held the Ingraham Professorship of Theology at Claremont School of Theology and the Avery Professorship at Claremont Graduate University.

John Beames was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Merchant Taylors' School, the East India Company College, and Haileybury and Imperial Service College. He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1858 to 1893.

A linguist and Indologist, Gilchrist studied at the Royal High School and the University of Edinburgh. He served as principal of Fort William College and held posts at the East India Company, its college, and University College London.
John Bray works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied under Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang and has held a post at the International Association for Ladakh Studies.
John Briggs was an Indologist and historian who studied at Eton College until 1799. He later served with the East India Company from around 1801 to 1835.

Indologist John Brockington studied at the University of Oxford, receiving an MA and DPhil. He served at the University of Edinburgh, where he was attested as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit in 1987 and Emeritus Professor of Sanskrit from 1998 to 2003.

John Brough, an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar, studied under Arthur Berriedale Keith at Edinburgh and Harold Walter Bailey at St John's College. He was Professor of Sanskrit at SOAS (1948–1967) and Professor at Cambridge (1967–1984).
John Buescher is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia in 1982. He is attested as Director at Voice of America in 2001.

John Burnet was a scholar of philosophy who studied at the Royal High School, the University of Edinburgh, and Balliol College, Oxford. He held a post at the University of St Andrews from around 1892 to 1926.

John Burton-Page was an Indologist, historian, and linguist who studied at Oxford and the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute. He served as Lecturer and later Reader at SOAS University of London between 1950 and 1982.
John C. Huntington was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He served as a professor at Ohio State University, attested in 1987–1990 and 2000.

John C. Maraldo is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held posts at the University of North Florida, where he was attested in 1988 and as distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy in 2015.

John Campbell Oman was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He worked for the Public Works Department, was a professor at Government College University, Lahore (1877–1897), and served as principal of Khalsa College (1898–1899).
John Capper was an Indologist and historian who founded The Ceylon Magazine in 1840. He served as editor of the Ceylon Times from 1858 to 1874.
John Carnac Morris was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the East India Company College from 1815 to 1817. He joined the Madras Civil Service in 1818.
John Caspar Leyden was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh from around 1790 to 1797. In 1808, he became professor of Hindustani at Fort William College.

John Chadwick was a linguist and historian who studied at Corpus Christi College and the University of Cambridge. He worked on the Oxford Latin Dictionary and served as Reader in Classics and Fellow at Downing College, Cambridge.

John Clark Archer was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Hiram College and Yale University. He held multiple academic posts at Yale from 1914 to 1950, including Hocker Professor of Comparative Religion.
John Clark Marshman worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He founded Serampore College in 1818 and directed the affairs of the Serampore Mission starting in 1819.

John Claude White worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Rugby School and the Royal Indian Engineering College before joining the Bengal Public Works Department as an Assistant Engineer in 1876.
